requirement:
> `Close a delivered search and record dependencies for snippets you used to
> justify your conclusion without an additional source read. search_id is the
> result's UUID and used is an array of its short entry tags, e.g.
> {"search_id":"11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111","used":["1"]}. Entries
> whose source you also read may be omitted; including them is harmless. Use
> used:[] when no entries qualify, including an empty search. Every delivered
> search must be finished before submission. The result is {search_id,
> finished:true}; no additional source is delivered.`
rationale: Add a test, marked {test}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.mcp.description`, that takes the `finish_search` entry from `ProjectSources` session `definitions()` and asserts its `description` is exactly the quoted text in the requirement. The natural place is `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]`, next to `search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot`, which already fetches that definition. — The requirement fixes the full text of the `finish_search` tool description. The only reviewed test that fetches the definition, `search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot`, asserts `parameters["required"]`, `properties.search_id` and `properties.used`. It never reads `description`, and it has no {test} reference to this requirement. A search of `crates` for description assertions found only the unrelated `lookup` check in `configured.rs`. The implementation in `definitions` could drop or reword any clause and every reviewed test would still pass. Examples are the UUID example, "Entries whose source you also read may be omitted", "Use used:[] ...", "Every delivered search must be finished", and the result shape `{search_id, finished:true}`. No testing exemption applies, because the text is a stated output that tests can check directly.

output.rationale:
The requirement `requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.mcp.description` is the text of the `finish_search` MCP tool description. It names no library, algorithm, signature, type or delegation interface. Every clause describes what the tool's consumer sees.

The clauses I checked were the description string itself, the `search_id` and `used` argument shapes in the example, and "The result is {search_id, finished:true}; no additional source is delivered". Any implementation that exposes the same description and arguments, and returns the same result, meets them. For example, the description could live in a constant, a generated schema or a different module and nothing observable would change. So these clauses are discretionary and not structural obligations.

The supplied root is `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#impl[Session<'_, D>/ToolSession<D>]/fn[definitions]`. It emits the `FINISH_SEARCH` tool definition with this exact description text. Its parameters are an object with `search_id` as a uuid-format string and `used` as an array of strings. Both are required and `additionalProperties` is false. That is consistent with the text and carries the {impl} marker. No further implementation root is needed, and no gap was found.
